name: Pivoting of graph states
summary: Hadamards on two adjacent vertices of a graph state and Z on their common neighbours implement a pivot of the graph.
description:
The *pivot* $G\wedge uv$ of a graph along an edge $uv$ is the local complementation $G\star u\star v\star u$. Write $A$ for the neighbours of only $u$, $B$ for the neighbours of only $v$ and $C$ for the common neighbours. The pivot toggles every edge between two vertices from different sets among $A$, $B$, $C$, and exchanges $u$ and $v$: in $G\wedge uv$, $u$ is connected to $B\cup C$ and $v$ to $A\cup C$.

On graph states, $|G\wedge uv\rangle = H_u H_v \prod_{w\in C} Z_w\,|G\rangle$. Duncan and Perdrix showed that when $u$ and $v$ have no common neighbours this follows from the generalised bialgebra rule alone, but that the general case needs an extra axiom (the H-loop axiom, see [Hadamard self-loop removal](../hadamard-self-loop-removal/)), which in turn follows from the [Euler decomposition](../euler-decomposition-hadamard/). This equation is the basis of the graph-like [pivot simplification](../pivot/).
parameter_notes: Shown for one neighbour of only u (a), one shared neighbour (c) and one neighbour of only v (b). The same holds for any sets of neighbours and any further vertices.
